displayName: Eduvora push scheduler — minute pinger attempt failed (log-based)

documentation.subject: [Eduvora] Cloud Scheduler logged a failed attempt for push-scheduler-minute
documentation.content:
## What fired

Cloud Scheduler wrote a **WARNING/ERROR execution log** for job **push-scheduler-minute** — i.e. an attempt at `GET https://eduvora.app/api/cron/subscription-renewals` did not succeed. Successful attempts log at `INFO` (`...AttemptFinished` with `httpRequest.status: 200`); anything at `WARNING` or above is a failed attempt.

This is the log-based twin of `ops/cloud-scheduler-alert-policy.json`. Use it when the metric-based policy cannot be created in your project (`cloudscheduler.googleapis.com/*` is absent from the public metrics catalog), or alongside it.

## Triage

1. Read the failing entries:
   `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_scheduler_job" resource.labels.job_id="push-scheduler-minute" severity>=WARNING' --limit=10 --freshness=30m --project=my-website-761e9 --format='table(timestamp, httpRequest.status, jsonPayload.status, jsonPayload.@type)'`
2. `401` → the `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>` header no longer matches Vercel's `CRON_SECRET`; re-run `ops/setup-cloud-scheduler.sh` with the current secret. `503` → `CRON_SECRET` is missing on Vercel. `504`/`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` → the function overran its 60s budget. No entries at all → the job is paused or deleted.
3. Confirm the endpoint really ran: Firestore → `settings/pushSchedulerState` → `lastRunAt` advances every minute.

A log-based alerting policy can hold only ONE condition, so this file deliberately watches failures only; use the metric policy (or the console job page) for the "no executions at all" case.

Full walkthrough: `ops/cloud-scheduler-setup.md`.
